title: Abu Bakr's inaugural
hookLine: I'm not the best of you: help me if I do right, correct me if I do wrong
tomorrow: two friends, one argument, and you're the judge. now what?

lines: THE SCRATCH OF A RED PEN.
cards: Red ink across an essay stings, even when every mark is right. The scratch of the pen, the circled word, the note in the margin. Plenty of us hand in our work hoping for a clean page.
When Abu Bakr stood up as leader after the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, he did something else on his first day. He handed the people the red pen, and asked them to use it on him.

teach.b: The speech is kept in Ibn Hisham's edition of Ibn Ishaq's life of the Prophet. Abu Bakr says: I have been given authority over you, and I am not the best of you.

teach.h: HELP ME, OR SET ME RIGHT.
teach.b: If I do well, help me. If I do wrong, set me right. Truthfulness is a trust, and lying is a betrayal.

teach.h: THE WEAK STRONG, THE STRONG WEAK.
teach.b: The weak among you is strong in my eyes until I secure his right, and the strong among you is weak in my eyes until I take from him what he owes.
Obey me as long as I obey God and his Messenger; if I disobey, you owe me no obedience. Hear what he's doing. No plan, no boast.
He names the limit of his own power, out loud, before anyone asks.

His Arabic for set me right is qawwimuni: straighten me, the way you'd straighten something bent. Feel the weight of that picture in your hand: a crooked stick, held and pressed until it runs true. He expects to bend.
He asks the crowd to do the pressing. Being corrected still stings. He asked for it anyway, at the very start, and named the people he'd protect: the weak, until they had their right.

how: Muslim teachers retell Abu Bakr's speech when they speak about leadership, accountability and consultation, often alongside the Qur'an's call to take counsel together.

games.q: Abu Bakr's speech — tap the pairs.

s: Abu Bakr opened by telling the people he was the best of them
he said the opposite: I am not the best of you.
he said the people owed him no obedience if he disobeyed God
obey me as long as I obey God and his Messenger.
he said the strong would be weak in his eyes until they paid what they owed
and the weak strong, until he secured their right.

games.q: you're the new shift lead at the coffee shop. on day one, which sentence fits Abu Bakr?
o: if I get something wrong, tell me. I'd rather know.
I've got this, so trust me and don't second-guess.
let's vote on everything, so nobody has to lead.
games.why: he led, and still asked to be set right: help me if I do well, correct me if I do wrong.

practice: Hold out one open hand, palm up, as if offering someone your pen. Let the arm rest, and keep the hand open. With each breath out, say inside: correct me.
When the words start to feel uncomfortable, keep the hand open anyway.

wordCard.voice: Abu Bakr's inaugural: his speech on taking office, asking the people to help him when right and set him straight when wrong.

orig.note: Arabic: qawwimuni, straighten me, set me right: Abu Bakr's word in the speech.

carryVoice: Carry this: correct me, said out loud before anyone has to say it to you. Day 1642, straightened.
